method: Each automatic match and each miss was checked by reading the finding's evidence against the defect description, after the sealed list was opened.

decisions.reason: The post-prediction-time probe removed lab records only; it says nothing about future admissions counted in prior_admissions_365d. No finding points at this defect.
Wrong pairing by the matcher. The real evidence is F02 temporal_leakage: deleting labs charted after discharge lowered test AUROC from 0.832 to 0.798 (95% CI of the drop 0.022 to 0.046).
F01 patient_overlap: 940 of 1,197 test patients also appear in training. The matcher had given that finding to B02.
F08: reported n 6,876 vs 1,719 rows in the predictions file; AUROC reported 0.878 vs 0.832 recomputed.
F03: 649 of 1,719 test scores differ between the validated pipeline and the inference command, consistent with missing labs filled with 0 at inference.
F04 to F07: Fahrenheit, umol/L, g/L and negative ages scored without error, which is the clipping behaviour.
F15 reports yaml imported in readmit/config.py line 5 and not declared; the sealed list located the same defect in requirements.txt.
A test assertion that is always true is not caught by any check; the mutation sample did not single it out.
The inference service reads 'threshold' from the model card with a 0.5 default. No check compared served alerts with the documented 0.35 threshold.
The follow-up exclusion function is called only from a unit test, so the unreferenced-code check did not flag it.

clean_twin_false_alarms: All 7 High findings on platform_b_clean come from the config-key check: it did not resolve a config section passed into a function under another name (model_cfg) and it treated a key written by the code itself (_root) as missing.

platform_a.note: Unlocated matches A02, A04, A05 were checked: temporal_leakage, train_serve_skew and metrics_not_reproducible each exist for them.
